adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38 — A Twilio outage or rate limit that lasts through two cron runs pushes every pending SMS reminder in the 7-day window past retryCount>1, and they are all hard-deleted with no log, alert, or backoff, so reminders are lost for good.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a `retryCount` column and increments it on scheduling failure (both in the `else` branch and in `catch`). At the start of each run it now calls `deleteMany` with `OR: [{ method: SMS, scheduledDate <= now }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]`, meaning any reminder whose `retryCount` reaches 2 will be hard-deleted (regardless of method/date) before it can be retried again. In a prolonged Twilio failure across multiple cron runs, reminders will be incremented to 2 and then deleted on the next run, permanently losing them with no logging/alert/backoff in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` both in the `else` branch and inside the `catch` block without any guarding `try/catch`. If that update throws (e.g., Prisma P2025 if the reminder row no longer exists, or any DB error), the exception will propagate out of the `catch` and abort the loop/handler. This failure mode is newly introduced by the added retryCount update logic in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — The catch block also counts a failed post-send DB update (line 169) as a send failure: the SMS is already queued at Twilio but referenceId is never saved, so the next run schedules it again (duplicate SMS) and the row is then deleted, leaving uncancellable Twilio messages behind.

adjudication.rationale: In the try block, after a successful Twilio schedule ("scheduledSMS.sid" truthy), the code performs a DB update to mark the reminder scheduled and save "referenceId". If that DB update fails, the catch block runs and only increments "retryCount" (it does not persist the Twilio sid or mark the reminder as scheduled). On the next run, the reminder can be treated as unscheduled again and re-sent, causing duplicate Twilio messages; then the new cleanup logic deletes rows with "retryCount > 1", which can remove the reminder record while already-queued Twilio messages remain without a saved referenceId.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 — The catch-block prisma update is unguarded, so if it throws (e.g. the reminder was deleted concurrently by a booking cancellation, P2025, or a DB error) the exception escapes the loop, aborts processing of all remaining reminders, and the cron returns 500.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` inside the `catch` block (and also in the `else` path) without any guarding try/catch. If that update throws (e.g., record not found/P2025 due to concurrent deletion, or any DB error), the exception will propagate out of the loop/handler and abort processing remaining reminders, causing the API/cron to fail. Previously the catch only logged, so this failure mode is introduced by the change.

adjudication.rationale: In the per-reminder `try { ... } catch` block, the Twilio scheduling and the subsequent `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ referenceId: scheduledSMS.sid })` are within the same `try`. If Twilio succeeds (SMS scheduled) but the DB update fails, control goes to `catch`, which unconditionally increments `retryCount` instead of persisting `referenceId`. Since the diff also adds deletion of reminders with `retryCount > 1` in `deleteMany({ where: { OR: [...] }})`, this can lead to the reminder being deleted while the SMS remains scheduled in Twilio with no stored `referenceId` (and thus no way to cancel via this record).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — retryCount is set from a stale value read earlier (`reminder.retryCount + 1`) and not with an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`, so overlapping cron runs lose increments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `retryCount` and updates it via `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` in two places (the `else` branch after attempting to schedule, and in the `catch`). Since `reminder.retryCount` is read earlier from `findMany(...)` and then written back later, concurrent/overlapping executions of this handler can perform lost updates (both read the same value and both write back `+1`). The diff does not use Prisma’s atomic `{ increment: 1 }`, so the finding is grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:38 — Reminders that exhaust retries are silently hard-deleted with no log, alert, or failure record, so users never learn their SMS reminder was dropped.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a cleanup `deleteMany` that hard-deletes any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1` (regardless of method or date) via an `OR` clause, and there is no logging/alerting/failure persistence around that deletion. Failed scheduling increments `retryCount` (in both the `else` and `catch` paths), so reminders that exceed the threshold will be removed on a later run without any explicit record of why they were dropped. This is an observability/product concern grounded in the new logic, though the diff alone doesn’t prove it violates intended requirements.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 — retryCount is written as a stale read-modify-write (reminder.retryCount + 1) rather than an atomic { increment: 1 }, so overlapping cron runs lose increments and the retry bound drifts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `retryCount` is incremented via a read-modify-write using the previously selected value (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) in both the `else` branch and the `catch` block. If multiple handler/cron executions process the same reminder concurrently, later updates can overwrite earlier ones (lost update), so `retryCount` may not reflect the true number of failures and the `deleteMany` condition `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` can be delayed/incorrect. An atomic Prisma update (`{ increment: 1 }`) would avoid this.
